title: Leaders of Old
subtitle: Remembering the figures who guided the community
body: Across generations, Murle communities have been guided by respected figures whose wisdom, courage, and fairness earned them lasting recognition. These leaders were rarely chosen by birthright alone; standing within the community was earned through demonstrated judgment and service.

Spiritual leaders, age-set representatives, and clan elders each played distinct roles in maintaining order, resolving disputes, and guiding important community decisions such as the timing of migrations or responses to conflict.

Stories of these leaders are often woven into songs and proverbs, preserving their memory long after their lifetimes. They serve as models of the values the community continues to hold dear: patience, courage, and care for the collective good.
This section will grow over time as more histories are gathered and verified with community elders.
